title: Recommend Cheapest Reply Time for Active Threads
prompt: A community forum tracks threads and member reply activity. The `threads` table records each thread's `thread_id`, `title`, `category`, and `is_active` flag (TRUE when the thread is open for discussion, FALSE when archived or locked). The `reply_times` table logs every member's reply to a thread, recording `reply_id`, `thread_id`, `member_id`, and `response_minutes` (how many minutes after the thread was created that member posted their reply). You need to find, for each active thread (`is_active = TRUE`), the fastest reply time across all members—that is, the minimum `response_minutes` for that thread. Threads that are NOT active (where `is_active = FALSE`) should be excluded from the output entirely. Return one row per active thread showing `thread_id`, `title`, and `fastest_reply_minutes` (the minimum `response_minutes` for that thread). Order the result by `thread_id` ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE threads (thread_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE reply_times (reply_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, thread_id INTEGER NOT NULL, member_id INTEGER NOT NULL, response_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL);

composite_moves: join threads to reply_times on thread_id
look up is_active gate from threads
WHERE gate: is_active = TRUE (exclude non-active threads)
GROUP BY thread_id, title to aggregate the minimum

hints: You need to combine information from both tables using the shared thread_id key.
Only include threads where is_active is TRUE; use a WHERE clause to filter before or after the join.
For each active thread, find the smallest response_minutes across all its replies—GROUP BY and an aggregate function will help.
answer_key: SELECT t.thread_id, t.title, MIN(rt.response_minutes) AS fastest_reply_minutes FROM threads t INNER JOIN reply_times rt ON t.thread_id = rt.thread_id WHERE t.is_active = TRUE GROUP BY t.thread_id, t.title ORDER BY t.thread_id;

_meta.scenario: a community forum tracking thread participation and member retention
